title: Boaz Gaon turned his father's illness into Wisdo, an app that connects people in crisis and reduces loneliness

trailer.text: Boaz Gaon, who has a background in journalism and storytelling, founded Wisdo, an Israeli mental wellness startup, together with Ido Engel.
According to NoCamels, he drew inspiration from the loss of his father, Israeli businessman and philanthropist Benny Gaon, who died in 2008.
Gaon explains that the goal is to help people thrive through life's painful moments by connecting to people who have already been through them.
According to the company, over 90 percent of those who downloaded the app have been matched with people going through the same or a similar experience.
According to MedCity News, in a study with Humana, 58% of Medicare Advantage participants reported less loneliness after three months.

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: 2019 Google Play Award, Apple's app of the day

paragraphs.text: According to ISRAEL21c, Boaz Gaon's father was diagnosed with cancer in 2000, and he died eight years later.
According to NoCamels, the father was Israeli businessman and philanthropist Benny Gaon, and he died in 2008.
According to MedCity News, Boaz was his father's primary caretaker.
Gaon said the family felt it was difficult to impossible to find people who had been down the same path, who could be emotionally supportive and who were available.
According to the Jerusalem Post, despite the father's knowledge and connections, the family made hundreds of mistakes which, had they been avoided, might have lessened his suffering.
Gaon said that Wisdo grew out of his personal experience when his father was diagnosed with cancer.
According to ISRAEL21c, the idea for the app came to him already then, in 2000.
According to NoCamels, he founded Wisdo in 2015 together with Ido Jonathan Engel.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the two set out to build a sort of Waze of life, a platform that helps people navigate life transitions and challenges.
Gaon explained that the mission is to help people thrive through life's painful moments by connecting to people who have already been through them.
He said the dream is an app that everyone has on their phone and that helps them thrive through everything they go through in life.
Gaon said that a generation that grew up connected to 3.5 billion people through the Internet still feels that no one understands it.
According to him, most users are young people, and social media use can leave people lonelier than ever.
According to TechCrunch, a recent study showed a causal relationship between social media use and depression and loneliness.
According to a JMIR study, Medicare spends $6.7 billion a year due to social isolation.
In 2023, then-U.S. Surgeon General Vivek Murthy declared loneliness a public health epidemic.
Users choose steps within an experience to find the exact stage they are at.
According to Fierce Healthcare, Wisdo uses AI based on 100 million peer interactions to match members with the right support.
The app is restricted to those over the age of 17.
According to NoCamels, the community is almost entirely self-managed, and this is what sets the platform apart.
Badge holders are mentored for 30 days before taking on a new role, and also receive monthly training for crisis situations.
According to ISRAEL21c, moderators closely supervise the community, ensuring that no harmful content is uploaded and that cases requiring the involvement of authorities are dealt with offline.
According to Gaon, the moderators receive an automatic notification when someone mentions a keyword from a watchlist.
The company is mostly based in Ramat Gan, and includes mobile developers and content and marketing people.
According to ISRAEL21c, the company first raised money about three years before the article, and planned further funding rounds in early 2019.
According to TechCrunch, Wisdo raised $11 million in seed funding from a small number of angel investors.
Wisdo's chairman is Dr. Richard Klausner, who was previously director of the U.S. National Cancer Institute.
According to TechCrunch, Wisdo built a timeline of steps and, in its beta version, grew to 500 thousand users.
According to ISRAEL21c, most users come from English-speaking countries.
According to the Jerusalem Post, hundreds of thousands of people have anonymously mapped themselves to more than 15 million life steps.
According to the company, over 90 percent of those who downloaded the app have been matched with people going through the same or a similar experience.
An internal Wisdo study of more than 7,600 members showed that users' perceived social isolation dropped by more than 15 percent within two weeks.

According to a NoCamels article from May 2019, in March of that year Wisdo announced a collaboration with the Center for Advanced Hindsight at Duke University on a study presented as the first large-scale study of the effect of emotional well-being networks on loneliness and isolation.

A column in the Jerusalem Post claimed that Dr. Lior Tzoref conducted in-depth research that proved, according to the writer, that Wisdo is effective in reducing loneliness, that is, in reducing the feeling of social isolation.
Jennifer Sapir of Humana said that during the coronavirus period, Medicare Advantage members were lonely, and this became a problem.
According to Managed Healthcare Executive, a yearlong study with Humana included almost 1,400 Medicare Advantage members aged 65 and older.
According to MedCity News, after three months 58% of participants reported less loneliness.
There was a 10% decrease in inpatient visits, 4% in ER visits and 6% in urgent care visits.
92% of participants said they would recommend Wisdo, and about 42% of users were still accessing it a year after joining.
In the JMIR study in Colorado, 815 ethnically and socially diverse participants completed registration.
After 90 days, there was a 14.6% decrease in loneliness, 50.1% in depression symptoms and 29% in anxiety symptoms.
90% of participants were engaged after 60 days, and 86% after 90 days.
A later study included 243 of 1,104 enrollees, and reported significant improvements in loneliness (11.1%) and depression (28.3%).
According to NoCamels, Wisdo won a 2019 Google Play Award.
According to the Jerusalem Post, it was selected as Apple's app of the day and received excellent reviews from thankful users.
Online therapy company Talkspace signed a partnership with Wisdo, focused on improving access to mental health resources for people aged 65 and older.
A year later, Talkspace acquired Wisdo Health, to integrate peer support and coaching into its services.
Wisdo CEO Ron Goldman said that joining with Talkspace would make it possible to bring the power of peer support to more people.

stations.title: What the studies did not prove

paragraphs.text: The Colorado study had no control group, and its statistical power was limited by the number of participants who completed the surveys at all time points.
All of its participants were adults from Colorado, and the authors wrote that future studies should examine geographically diverse populations.
The study disclosed a conflict of interest: four of the authors were employees of, consultants to, or board members of Wisdo.
In the later study too, the researchers noted that the analysis was limited by the lack of a control group and the brevity of the mental health measures.
This study was funded by Wisdo Health.
The figure on reduced isolation within two weeks also comes from an internal Wisdo study.
